system_overview: This specification models Lamport's distributed mutual-exclusion algorithm, which appeared as an example in the foundational paper 'Time, Clocks and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System' (Communications of the ACM, volume 21, number 7, pages 558-565, 1978). The algorithm allows a set of processes to coordinate access to a critical section using logical clocks and message passing over pairwise FIFO communication channels, without relying on shared memory.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a parameterized number of processes. Each process has its own local logical clock and communicates with every other process through dedicated point-to-point FIFO message channels. Three types of messages are exchanged: request messages (carrying the sender's clock value), acknowledgment messages, and release messages.
state_variables: The system tracks five pieces of state: (1) a local clock value for each process, (2) a table recording the clock value associated with each request that each process has received from every other process (zero if no pending request), (3) a set of acknowledgments each process has collected from other processes, (4) the message queues for every ordered pair of processes representing the pairwise FIFO network, and (5) the set of processes currently in the critical section.
initial_state: All process clocks start at one. No requests have been recorded (all entries are zero). No acknowledgments have been collected (all sets are empty). All message channels are empty. No process is in the critical section.
actions: A process can perform one of six actions: (1) Request access to the critical section by recording its own clock value and broadcasting a request to all other processes. (2) Receive a request from another process, record the request's clock value, update the local clock to be at least one more than the received clock, and send an acknowledgment back. (3) Receive an acknowledgment from another process and add that process to the acknowledgment set. (4) Enter the critical section, which requires having received acknowledgments from all processes and having a request with higher priority (lower clock, with process identifier as tiebreaker) than all other pending requests. (5) Exit the critical section by broadcasting a release message, clearing the process's own request, and resetting its acknowledgment set. (6) Receive a release message from another process and clear that process's request record.
safety_properties: The primary safety property is mutual exclusion: at most one process may be in the critical section at any given time. Additionally, a type correctness invariant ensures all variables remain within their expected domains, and a bounded network property states that no communication channel ever contains more than three messages.
model_bounds: The specification parameterizes the number of processes and includes a maximum clock bound used as a state constraint for finite-state model checking. Clock values must not exceed this bound during exploration.
additional_assumptions: Communication channels are pairwise FIFO: messages between any pair of processes are delivered in the order they were sent. The algorithm relies on Lamport's logical clock mechanism to establish a total ordering of events across the distributed system.
